9.10.1. qnav.simulation.simulation

9.10.1.1. simulation.py

summary:

The core harness responsible for coordinating simulations. This module contains the core functionalities for managing simulations. This mostly revolves around a core loop and the scheduling of sensor time intervals, sensor measurements and data fusion.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation.

qnav.simulation.simulation.run_simulation_loop(trajectory: ~qnav.waypoints.trajectory.Trajectory, estimated_state: ~qnav.estimation.state.EstimatedState, hardware: ~typing.Collection[~qnav.measurement.sensor.SensorFusion], clock: ~qnav.measurement.clock.Clock = <qnav.measurement.clock.DummyClock object>, results: ~qnav.simulation.results.ResultsCapture = <qnav.simulation.results.CaptureAll object>, displayer: ~qnav.simulation.display.Display = <qnav.simulation.display.ConsoleDisplay object>)[source]

Executes the full simulation loop from start to finish. On succession returns states and results in requested format.

Parameters:

  • trajectory (Trajectory) – The trajectory to draw ground truth records from. This is what the virtual platform is to follow.

  • estimated_state (EstimatedState) – The initial estimated state. This will be updated throughout the simulation via fusion.

  • hardware (Collection[SensorFusion]) – A collection of SensorFusion instances. This represents the hardware and fusion algorithms attached to the virtual platform.

  • clock – A virtual clock added to simulate clock errors. This is used when virtual clock drift is required.

  • results – The results capture instance used to manage result data. This controls how and what data is collected throughout the simulation.

  • displayer – The displayer instance used for displaying progress. This presents a display of the ongoing simulation allowing for immediate feedback of its progress.
